children: Uruguay’s trade balance swung to a deficit of $42.8 million in August 2026 from a surplus of $322.49 million a year earlier.
Imports surged 24.3% year-on-year to $1.06 billion, led by a 42.2% increase in purchases of intermediate goods, driven by a 558% jump in oil and distillate imports.
Consumer goods imports rose 17.1%, with purchases of autos and other transport equipment increasing 47.2%, while capital goods imports declined 11.3%.
Meanwhile, exports fell 13.4% to $1.02 billion as sales of primary goods slumped 37.3%, with agriculture and livestock products down 40.6%.
In contrast, manufacturing exports rose 1.6%, while utility exports increased 56.6%.

title: Uruguay Trade Balance Swings to Deficit in August
